sections.heading: Principle
sections.body: A public offer is governed by ss 23 to 42. Misstatement attracts criminal liability under s. 34 and civil liability under s. 35.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: Prospectus contents are s. 26. Deemed prospectus is s. 25. Shelf and red herring prospectus are ss 31 and 32. A statement must be untrue or misleading, or an omission must be matters required, for liability. Defences include belief on reasonable grounds and withdrawal of consent. Expert statements need consent under s. 26.

caseLaw.name: Derry v Peek
caseLaw.point: A false statement in a prospectus is fraudulent only if made knowingly, without belief in its truth, or recklessly. Statutory liability under sections 34 and 35 does not require that common-law fraud finding.
